requirement_title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283
Type: bug

## Requirement

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with no generated resolver at all. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime.

Repro: two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`.

Expected: a clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

Actual:

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8.

What triggers it (`Item` declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`):

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

It needs all three of: generic, value type, from a referenced assembly. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` makes the crash disappear.

Reporter's analysis: `CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly, so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` like the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers. That collection is empty for a metadata symbol. The reporter did not narrow down which of the three fires.

Workaround: `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` before `GetObjectInfo` is reached.

## Acceptance criteria

- Building `app` from the repro produces no CS8785 warning. (derived)
- Building `app` from the repro produces no AD0001 warning from `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer`. (derived)
- `app.dll` contains a `GeneratedMessagePackResolver` (a generated resolver exists). (derived)
- The generator and analyzer do not throw on a closed generic struct or record struct declared in a referenced assembly.
- Closed generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same assembly keep working as before (the "ok" rows in the table). (derived)
- Diagnostics that need a source location do not crash when the offending symbol has no declaring syntax (metadata symbol). (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue. The reporter points at `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` being indexed unguarded at TypeCollector.cs lines 735, 1009 and 1101, and notes the neighbouring helpers use `FirstOrDefault()`. Possibly related: #2092 (CS8785 from the v3 generator, different inner exception, no repro).
verdict_reason: 1 test(s) fail on head (passing on base, or added by the change): GenericsFormatterTests.ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember

checked.what: Existing SourceGenerator tests on head: 169/170 passed, 1 failed
Existing SourceGenerator tests on base: 167/167 passed, 0 failed

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: The new filter ReportIfLocatedInCompilation silently drops every diagnostic whose location is in a syntax tree outside the compilation, and GetPropertyIdentifierLocation now returns null for metadata symbols. This matches L8, which says a type from a referenced assembly is deliberately not analysed and that a missing diagnostic for it is not a defect. The README and MsgPack004 doc text saying such diagnostics belong to the defining assembly is consistent with L8, so it is not a problem.

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: The generated resolver for the consuming assembly may not include a formatter for the closed generic Item<int>. L11, L12 and L13 say to follow the requirement, which only asks for a clean build and a generated resolver, so the tests asserting only that the resolver hint name exists are acceptable.
Receipts/ClosedGenericStructFromReferencedAssemblyTests.cs: requirement test fails on base (4/4), passes on head (4/4); refutes 2 lens claim(s): requirement-tests-1, requirement-tests-2
Receipts/MetadataGenericStructDiagnosticLeakTests.cs: edge-case test fails on head: 1/1 failed
Mutation not meaningful: the selected tests already fail on head

findings.claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops a diagnostic only when its location is in source but in another syntax tree. A metadata member has no declaring syntax, so the changed MemberNeedsKey site now builds its diagnostic with a null location (Location.None). IsInSource is false for that location, so the filter lets it through. Concrete input: the referenced assembly defines `[MessagePackObject] public struct Item<T> { public int Value; }` (built without the analyzer, or with MsgPack004 suppressed), and the app has a member of type `Item<int>`. On head the analyzer reports MsgPack004, an Error per L2, with no location in the consuming compilation, so a build that only crashed with warnings on base now fails. This contradicts L8 (metadata types are deliberately not diagnosed by the consumer) and the helper's own remark that such problems are dropped. The same leak applies with AllowPrivate=true, where metadata backing fields such as `<Key>k__BackingField` are private fields without [Key].

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.MetadataGenericStructDiagnosticLeakTests.NoMsgPackDiagnosticsForClosedGenericStructFromReferencedAssembly. It compiles lib to an image reference, runs all MessagePack analyzers on the app compilation and expects no MsgPack*/AD0001 diagnostics. On head it fails with a location-less MsgPack004 for Item<int>.Value.

hunches.claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation only drops diagnostics whose location is in source of another compilation. Diagnostics with no location (Location.None, from FirstOrDefault() null) pass the filter (IsInSource is false). Diagnostics for metadata-only closed generic structs (MsgPack004 MemberNeedsKey, MsgPack003 etc.) are therefore still reported with no location in users' builds, so a defining assembly's non-annotated members could surface as new location-less errors/warnings in the consuming project. MsgPack004 is an Error (L2), so a previously silent build (generator crashed) may now fail. The filter condition is inverted relative to its doc comment.

receipt_plan.detail: Analyzer test: lib defines generic struct Item<T> with a public member lacking [Key] and [IgnoreMember]; app has [MessagePackObject] Cmd with Item<int> member. Assert no MsgPack004/MsgPack003 diagnostics are reported in app. Expect failure due to Location.None diagnostics passing the filter.

hunches.claim: The wrapper only affects the analyzer callback path. The reporting of diagnostics is wrapped, but the actual crash sites in GetObjectInfo for metadata symbols (the other DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] sites noted by reporter, around line 735 and similar) are not changed in the diff. If any remain, the IndexOutOfRange still fires for closed generic structs. Also, the generator path passes null reportDiagnostic, so the guard does nothing there. The requirement's CS8785 fix depends on the remaining sites being safe.

receipt_plan.detail: Generator test with the two-project repro (lib Item<T> record struct/struct, app Cmd with Item<int>). Assert no CS8785 and that GeneratedMessagePackResolver is emitted; also run the analyzer for AD0001.

hunches.claim: Closed generic metadata structs would now be fully analyzed and could generate a formatter in the consuming assembly, a generated-output change for users with Item<T> from referenced assemblies. Existing 'ok' cases such as class Item<T> should remain byte-identical in the generated output.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun generator snapshot tests for generic class from referenced assembly and non-generic struct cases; confirm no snapshot changes.

hunches.claim: The ReportIfLocatedInCompilation filter wrapper has no negative test: no test checks that a diagnostic on a source-located symbol in the compilation is still reported. If the guard is inverted or removed, tests with metadata types still pass because they only assert no diagnostics. Dropping all diagnostics (e.g. negating the condition) would not be caught either, since no test expects a diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1445 negate-condition: if (!diagnostic.Location.IsInSource || ContainsSyntaxTree(...)) -> if (diagnostic.Location.IsInSource && !ContainsSyntaxTree(...)); expected to survive because the added tests only assert zero diagnostics and no test expects a MsgPack diagnostic to still be reported for a same-assembly type.

hunches.claim: The MsgPack004 (MemberNeedsKey) change to FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation() is covered only by an assertion of no diagnostics. A mutation reverting to [0] would be caught only if that path is reached. The unkeyed-member test uses a public property on a metadata struct; whether the path is reached depends on earlier code, and the same-assembly MemberNeedsKey diagnostic is not re-asserted, so a regression that breaks location for source types would go unnoticed.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1077 delete-statement: FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation() -> null location; expected to survive because no test expects MsgPack004 at a specific location for source-declared members.

hunches.claim: No test exercises the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull path (GetPropertyIdentifierLocation) with a metadata type. The three new tests use valid [Key(n)] attributes, so line 985 is never reached for a metadata property. Reverting to DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] would not fail any test.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:985 delete-statement: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation(item) -> ((PropertyDeclarationSyntax)item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].GetSyntax()).Identifier.GetLocation(); expected to survive because no added test has a key attribute with null int and string key on a metadata type.

hunches.claim: The tests assert that the resolver hint name is generated, but never check that a formatter for the closed generic type (e.g. MyGenericStruct<int>) is in the output (SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck is set). The resolver could be generated without handling the generic member and the tests would still pass, so the requirement 'a generated resolver exists' is checked only at the weakest level.

receipt_plan.detail: TypeCollector closed-generic branch (CollectGeneric): delete-statement for the GetObjectInfo call on the metadata closed generic; expected to survive because tests only assert warnings are absent and the resolver hint name exists.

hunches.claim: The tests include no regression checks for the 'ok' rows: closed generic classes from metadata and non-generic structs. These are the rows that must keep working as before, but there is no test for them. A guard change that dropped them would go undetected.

receipt_plan.detail: TypeCollector.cs:1445 swap-boolean: return/skip all reports for metadata locations; expected to survive because no test covers class<T> or non-generic struct from metadata.

hunches.claim: The requirement names three unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites in GetObjectInfo (reported at 735, 1009 and 1101). The diff fixes only the two later ones (now ~985 and ~1077). Both shifted by 24 lines, so the first site sits at about line 711 on head and is not in any hunk. If that diagnostic path is reached for a closed generic value type from metadata, it still throws IndexOutOfRangeException. That would leave the acceptance criterion 'diagnostics that need a source location do not crash when the symbol has no declaring syntax' unmet.

receipt_plan.detail: grep `DeclaringSyntaxReferences\[0\]` in src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs on head. Any remaining hit inside GetObjectInfo is an unguarded index reachable for metadata symbols via CollectGeneric.
